summary: Reconcile an absolute freshness guarantee against a cache hit-rate budget and a frozen configuration contract.

contradictions.statement: Content can never be older than the latest publish, and self-inflicted cache misses are a defect — the seeded global flush satisfies the first by manufacturing the second, and nothing in the documents says how much cache the flush destroys.

ttl_seconds cannot both remain the mechanism that bounds staleness and stop being the mechanism that makes a publish visible; the configuration contract forbids resolving this by renaming or adding required keys.

hard_constraints.statement: A file containing only ttl_seconds and max_entries loads and works.
A read after a publish for that key never returns pre-publish content.
Publishing one key does not evict unrelated keys; they still serve without a store round-trip.
read(key, now) and publish(key, content, now) keep injected time; no clock reads.
max_entries still bounds the number of retained entries.

interacting_constraints_note: HC2 and HC3 are the interacting pair. The seeded implementation satisfies HC2 and violates HC3; a TTL-only cache satisfies HC3 and violates HC2. Neither document names the trade-off.

evidence.fact_only_available_there: 94.2% of documents are never republished after first publish and take 61% of reads, while the 0.8% hot set carries 71% of republishes at a mean of 12 per hot document per hour.
evidence.why_it_matters: The stakeholder documents establish that self-inflicted misses are undesirable, but not their scale. Only the telemetry shows that a global flush discards an overwhelmingly cold-but-still-correct cache to fix one document — the fact that makes per-key invalidation necessary rather than merely tidy.

acceptance_suite.note: N15 §6.4 — must-pass designation is pinned with the manifest. success = all must-pass green AND zero hard-constraint violations.

distractors.reading: Global flush on every write: the literal Editorial requirement. Never stale, and it evicts the 94.2% of the corpus the write did not touch.
TTL-only, no invalidation: the literal Platform requirement. Excellent hit rate, serves a retracted revision for the whole TTL window.

deliverables.description: The change satisfying the reconciled requirements.
Decision record: what was decided, alternatives rejected, and exactly what ttl_seconds now means.

calibration.solvability: sealed/reference passes the full suite; no LLM involved.
calibration.discrimination: PENDING — baseline saturation/floor check requires runs at both tiers (N15 §6.3(2)).
